title: Cricket's LBW Rule, Explained Simply

content: LBW stands for leg before wicket. A batter can be given out if the ball, without first hitting the bat, strikes the batter's body and would otherwise have gone on to hit the stumps.

Umpires consider where the ball pitched, where it hit the batter, and whether the ball was heading for the stumps. A ball that pitches outside the leg stump generally cannot result in an LBW decision.
Ball-tracking technology used in the Decision Review System helps check these questions, but the on-field umpire's original decision stands when the evidence is marginal.
